records.sourceFile: Substance misuse in elite athletes - Early detection, brief intervention and referral to treatment.pdf

paper.citation: McDuff DR, Garvin M, Chang J, Thompson D. Substance Misuse in Elite Athletes: Early Detection, Brief Intervention and Referral to Treatment. Clin Sports Med. 2023.
paper.abstract: This clinical review describes early detection, brief intervention and referral to treatment for alcohol, cannabis and tobacco/nicotine misuse in elite athletes. It highlights screening instruments, urine testing and brief motivational interventions, and the role of sports medicine staff in identifying misuse.
paper.tldr: Sports medicine staff and athletic trainers are well placed to spot alcohol, cannabis and nicotine misuse early through pre-season screening and brief motivational conversations. Referral to addiction treatment is appropriate when brief steps do not work.
paper.methods: Narrative clinical review. No systematic search method is described. The review draws on prevalence surveys, screening instruments and intervention studies in collegiate, professional and non-athlete samples.
paper.findings: Binge drinking, cannabis use and nicotine use are common in collegiate and professional athletes, and use is higher in some sports. Screening tools such as AUDIT, CAGE-AID, CUDIT-R or CUDIT-SF, and the Brief Young Adult Alcohol Consequences and Brief Marijuana Consequences Questionnaires, can help identify misuse. Brief motivational interventions with personalized feedback have shown benefit in some athlete and student samples, and in baseball players, brief tobacco interventions were followed by higher quit rates (23% vs 13% at 2 years in one trial of high school players).
paper.limitations: No search methods are described, so the evidence base cannot be reproduced. Many data sources are US collegiate surveys or non-athlete samples. The authors note that there are few recent brief-intervention studies for tobacco and limited data on current professional athletes.
paper.practicalImplications: Add alcohol, cannabis and tobacco/nicotine questions to the pre-season physical and repeat screens after injury, trade or other transitions. Where screens are positive, use brief motivational feedback and refer on to an addiction specialist if it does not work.
paper.athleteDev: Performance Application: Build screening into pre-season and transition routines, and train athletic trainers and coaches in brief motivational conversations. Keep counselling and referral pathways in place, since misuse can affect sleep, recovery, performance and injury risk.
paper.rtp: Return to Sport Application: This review does not address return to sport. It covers substance misuse screening and referral, and it does not evaluate whether misuse affects return-to-play decisions.
